idiom_name: creator functions returning an initialized struct, or a *_create() function returning an opaque handle
implementation_notes: C has no constructors, so the pattern is carried entirely by naming and call shape: give each construction route its own function (timespec_from_ms(), matrix_identity(), buffer_create_with_capacity()) and treat the returned struct or handle as the only way to obtain the object. For small, fully visible structs prefer returning by value - C99 compound literals keep the initializer compact - while opaque handles pair each *_create with a matching *_destroy so allocation and deallocation stay in the same translation unit. The classic structure is not optional here, but nothing in the language enforces it: the invariant that callers use the creators survives only through the naming convention and, for opaque types, through the header hiding the struct definition.
pitfalls: Out-parameter creators hand the caller a half-initialized object: if the function fails after allocating, the caller must not use or free the partial value - prefer returning by value, or document that the output is untouched on error.

Every creator needs a matching destructor: mixing stack values, malloc'd handles and static storage in one API makes the ownership pairing unverifiable, so keep *_create and *_destroy in the same translation unit.
Nothing stops a caller from filling a non-opaque struct directly; if the representation must stay under control, define the struct only in the .c file and expose a pointer to an incomplete type.
